memos.headline: Momentum leaders S02, S05, S08 stretched to overbought; S01 and S06 in persistent downtrends
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in the universe today. S02 (RSI 76.9, +23% vs 50d), S05 (RSI 70.2, +19% vs 50d), and S08 (RSI 75.7, at 52w high) are the strongest relative-strength names but all three are extended well above their moving averages, raising near-term mean-reversion risk. S10 and S07 offer better risk/reward: both are trending strongly above their 50d and 200d means with RSIs in the high-50s/mid-60s and only modest drawdowns from highs. On the weak side, S01 (RSI 41, -16.7% from high, -18.7% rel strength vs SPY over 12w) and S06 (RSI 41.5, -11% from high, -11.3% rel strength 12w) are in clear downtrends below both moving averages and I see no reason to step in front of that. I have highest conviction in S10 as a long—trend is intact, relative strength is strong, and RSI has room to run—while S01 is my strongest avoid.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Deliver Exceptional Earnings Power; S09 Margin Collapse Is a Red Flag
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe between companies with durable, expanding earnings power and those facing margin compression. S10 stands out with a 63.1% net margin, +73.2% YoY revenue growth, and near-doubled net income on just $8.47B of total debt — this is the cleanest earnings profile in the group. S05 is similarly compelling at 56.9% net margin with +81.2% YoY net income growth and minimal leverage ($14.79B debt). On the other end, S09 posted a 4.9% net margin with net income down 45.8% YoY on anemic 2.4% revenue growth — I cannot pay for that trajectory. S02 is similarly sluggish at 5.6% margin and flat earnings, though its $77.92B debt load makes it even less attractive. I would need to see margin stabilization and a return to earnings growth at S09 and S02 before reconsidering.

views.note: 63.1% net margin, +73.2% revenue growth, +94.5% net income growth, and only $8.47B debt — best earnings quality in the universe by a wide margin.
56.9% net margin with +81.2% YoY net income growth and low leverage at $14.79B debt signals durable, high-quality earnings.
38.3% net margin, +18.3% revenue growth, and +23.1% net income growth with manageable $40.26B debt — strong and consistent compounder.
Revenue of $181.52B growing 16.6% YoY with net income surging 76.7% suggests significant operating leverage, though 16.7% margin and $122.63B debt warrant monitoring.
Solid 22.2% revenue growth and 27.2% net income growth, but 14.6% margin and $36.21B debt on $17.41B revenue means leverage is elevated relative to earnings power.
Revenue of $111.18B growing 16.6% with 26.6% margin is respectable, but $82.70B total debt is heavy and net income growth of 19.4% only modestly outpaces the top line.
33.1% net margin is healthy but $448.76B total debt dwarfs revenue of $49.84B, and 10% revenue growth is the slowest among profitable names.
18.5% margin and 7.4% revenue growth are decent but unexciting; $23.85B debt on $21.23B quarterly revenue is manageable but growth is decelerating.
Net income collapsed 45.8% YoY to a 4.9% margin on barely growing revenue of $85.14B — classic cash-flow compression I refuse to pay for.
5.6% net margin, flat YoY earnings (-0.2%), 2.0% revenue growth, and $77.92B debt — no earnings momentum and heavy leverage.

memos.headline: Fed on Pause at 3.75% but Sticky 3.3% CPI and Rising Long Rates Argue Against Duration and Favor Defensive Positioning
memos.body: I see a clear pause regime: the fed funds upper bound has been flat at 3.75% for three months after 75 bps of cuts over the prior year, while CPI is running at 3.3% YoY—well above target and implying the Fed has limited room to ease further. The 10-year yield has surged 55 bps over three months to 4.59%, compressing the 10y-2y spread to just 47 bps, which signals the market is repricing for higher-for-longer rates and possibly a growth slowdown without the inflation relief needed for cuts. Unemployment at 4.3% is stable but has crept up 10 bps YoY, consistent with a late-cycle softening rather than outright recession. In this environment I favor banks (benefiting from a still-positive curve and stable short rates), staples (defensive in a slowdown), and energy (inflation hedge), while avoiding duration-sensitive growth names that are most vulnerable to the backup in long rates. A CPI print falling below 3.0% or unemployment jumping above 4.5% would shift my regime call toward imminent easing and flip me constructive on growth/duration.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth is the most exposed sector to the 55 bps backup in 10-year yields and a Fed stuck on pause with sticky inflation.
Banks benefit from a positively sloped curve (47 bps 10y-2y) and stable short rates in a pause regime with no imminent recession signal.
Staples offer defensive positioning as the labor market softens modestly and the Fed is unlikely to ease soon given 3.3% CPI.
Energy serves as a partial inflation hedge with CPI still at 3.3% YoY and the Fed unable to tighten further from here.
Broad cyclicals face mixed signals—stable employment supports demand but rising long rates and sticky inflation cap upside.
Rate-sensitive sectors face headwinds from the sharp rise in 10-year yields and a Fed unlikely to cut with inflation at 3.3%.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Split: S05 and S07 Surge While S04 Sinks — Momentum Fading Risk on Winners
memos.body: I am reading the earnings-season price reactions as the clearest sentiment signal across this universe. S05 (+10.0%) and S07 (+9.9%) posted the strongest positive reactions on their Q-results filings, but both are now two weeks past the catalyst and the follow-on 8-Ks (S05 Other Events 5/11, S07 board changes 4/10-4/13) do not suggest fresh positive narrative, raising the risk that the positive tone is already priced. S02 (+7.0% on 4/21) also had a strong beat reaction and followed up with a Reg FD disclosure on 5/11, which could sustain attention. On the negative side, S04 dropped -3.9% on earnings and then disclosed a director departure on 5/14 — a combination that signals deteriorating sentiment. S06 is the noisiest name with five 8-Ks in a month including bylaws amendments and material modifications to security-holder rights, yet its earnings reaction was a muted -0.8%, suggesting the market is uncertain and governance changes cloud the picture.

views.note: Massive +9.9% earnings pop signals a genuine narrative shift, though two weeks of digestion tempers my conviction.
+10.0% earnings reaction is the strongest in the universe but the 5/11 Other Events filing without further price data makes me slightly cautious on crowded positive tone.
+7.0% earnings reaction and a follow-up Reg FD disclosure suggest the company is actively managing the narrative upward.
Negative -3.9% earnings reaction compounded by a director departure the next day points to deteriorating sentiment trajectory.
High filing volume around governance changes and material rights modifications creates uncertainty; muted -0.8% earnings reaction suggests market is not rewarding the noise.
+3.2% earnings reaction is modestly positive but a preceding director change adds ambiguity; not enough signal to take a directional view.
-1.0% earnings reaction is mild but a director change four days later keeps sentiment murky.
Two director departure/appointment filings with no earnings reaction data leave me without a clear sentiment read.

memos.headline: WTI at $105 Signals Structural Energy-Supply Stress Despite Falling Policy Uncertainty
memos.body: I am focused on the 66% three-month surge in WTI crude to $104.66/bbl, which dwarfs the concurrent decline in the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index (down 40% over three months to 217) and the VIX retreat to 17.26. The divergence suggests the oil move is supply-driven—likely reflecting sanctions enforcement, OPEC discipline, or conflict-related disruption—rather than demand-pull, because credit spreads (HY OAS at 2.76%) and the yield curve (10y-2y at +0.47pp, flattening) are not signaling overheating. For the universe, energy-exposed names (S03, S09) should benefit structurally as long as supply constraints persist, while cost-sensitive industrials and consumer-facing names (S05, S06) face margin headwinds. I would change my view if sanctions are eased or OPEC signals a meaningful production increase, which would break the supply thesis. Confidence is moderate because the 8-K filings across the universe are Reg FD or Other Events disclosures without detail on content, limiting my ability to confirm company-specific geopolitical exposure.

views.note: Frequent Reg FD disclosures in April suggest active investor communication, likely around energy-market tailwinds from the 66% WTI surge.
Three 8-Ks since late March and the crude rally point to positive supply-side positioning; would reassess if sanctions relief materializes.
Rising energy input costs from $105 WTI create margin risk for cost-sensitive operations; recent 8-K offers no offsetting detail.
Three disclosures in five weeks amid surging oil prices suggest the company is managing headwinds; elevated crude is a structural drag until supply normalizes.
Active 8-K cadence but unclear geopolitical exposure; VIX and uncertainty declines are supportive but oil cost pass-through unknown.
Two Reg FD filings in April suggest proactive communication but without content detail I cannot assess geopolitical impact directionally.
